newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett says small percentage of cartridges fail.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett says small percentage of cartridges fail.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Thursday a small percentage of its black inkjet cartridges for printers sold in recent months produce fewer than the expected number of pages.
The company said it is offering to replace cartridges within three working days after customers call Hewlett-Packard.
Users may also return defective cartridges to their retailers, the company said.

Hewlett-Packard said the only affected cartridges are black inkjet cartridges compatible with DeskJet and DeskWriter 300, 500 and 600 series printers, Office Jet printer-fax-copier devices, HP FAX machines and DesignJet 200, 220 and 600 plotters. The company said one in 10 black cartridges with the following part numbers is affected: HP 51626A, HP 51629A and HP 51633M.
Hewlett-Packard said it discovered the problem in routine lab tests in May and took action immediately to correct it.
It said HP inkjet cartridges currently on store shelves are not affected and "a small percentage of customers who may have purchased cartridges a few months ago are noticing the failure."
Hewlett-Packard's stock fell 50 cents to $47.625 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
